deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is a financial or administrative memorandum: a record of numbers drawn in successive redemption lotteries (Auslosungen) of a bond issue headed 'Ostgoth.' Gauss is known to have kept careful records of his securities. The Roman numeral VIII likely marks the eighth drawing, but that reading is uncertain.

The drawings are semi-annual: 1850 1/11 (1 November 1850), 1851 1/5 (1 May 1851) and 1851 1/11 (1 November 1851). The next page continues with 1852 1/5. Each drawing is split into series A, B, C and D, and the drawn bond numbers are listed in ascending order.

The structure of each label is my inference, but every case on the page checks: the number before the letter equals the count of numbers drawn in that series.
- 1850 1/11: A has 5 numbers, B 12, C 12, D 13; total 42.
- 1851 1/5: A 5, B 12, C 13, D 13; total 43.
- 1851 1/11: A 6, B 11, C 13, D 13; total 43.
- The next page fits the same pattern: A 6, B 11, C 14, D 14; total 45.

The ranges of the numbers suggest series A has roughly 800 pieces and series B to D roughly 2000 each. That fits an amortization scheme in which each series is drawn roughly in proportion to its size; this too is my inference.

No computation is performed. Gauss is simply recording which bond numbers were called for repayment, presumably to check them against his own holdings. The underlinings (605 in 13D of 1850; a stroke under 772/1015 in 12C) may mark bonds that concern him; this is unverified.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible since there is no computation. Every series list is strictly increasing, and the count of numbers matches the numeric prefix in all twelve series, so the record is internally consistent.

transcription_corrections: In 12B of 1850/11, '1848/1923' is most likely two separate numbers, 1848 and 1923; the slash is probably just a separator stroke.
In 13C of 1851/5 the first entries are '44.378', i.e. 44 and 378. The cut-off '443' on the facing image is the same text, and the counts (13) and ascending order confirm the reading.
In 11B of 1851/11 the first number is 24, not 22 as the cut-off facing-page transcription has it.
In 5A of 1850/11, '626' is written with the final 6 overwritten, a correction; likewise the 9 in '1769' in 13D is retraced.
In 13C of 1851/11 a separator is missing between 338 and 439; they are two numbers.
The page header 'VIII' probably indexes the drawing or notebook section and is not part of the data; 'Ostgoth.' is the name of the loan or institution.
